summary: This script creates a new SQL Server database called MyDB with specific storage settings, then creates a simple two-column Person table inside it, and finally inserts two sample records into that table.

explanations.1: USE [master] switches to the master database, which is where you need to be to create a new database.
explanations.5: CONTAINMENT = NONE means this database doesn't use contained database authentication—users are managed at the server level instead.
explanations.7: The PRIMARY filegroup clause specifies where the main data file (.mdf) will be stored on disk, its starting size (8MB), and how much it can grow each time (64MB).
explanations.9: LOG ON specifies the transaction log file (.ldf) separately—this tracks all changes so SQL Server can recover from crashes; it has a 2TB max size limit.
explanations.10: CATALOG_COLLATION = DATABASE_DEFAULT means the system catalog (SQL Server's internal tables) will use the same character sorting rules as your user tables.
explanations.16: [dbo].[Person] creates a table in the dbo schema; brackets protect reserved words and special characters in names.
explanations.19: ON [PRIMARY] explicitly assigns this table to the primary filegroup we defined earlier.
explanations.22: The INSERT statement adds two complete rows at once using the VALUES clause with multiple row sets separated by commas.
